channel.title: Weekly Worker (unofficial)
channel.description: Unofficial RSS feed of articles published by Weekly Worker.

item.title: Challenging false assumptions
item.description: According to the standard Trotskyist narrative, the 1956 events in Hungary were an aborted political revolution. A comforting story that led them to celebrate the restoration of capitalism in eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union over 1989-91. Mike Macnair always had his doubts
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: Deterrents real and imagined
item.description: The present stand-off in the Gulf could run and run. Or there could be a sudden escalation. It is impossible to say, argues Yassamine Mather. Meanwhile, the situation inside Iran grows ever more desperate for working people
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Funny, if only
item.description: Anthropic’s initial public offering was the biggest in history. But the bumpy ride for tech stocks continues, as does political controversy over the AI industry. Paul Demarty investigates the bubble
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Health under attack
item.description: What lies behind the surge of measles cases in the USA? It is not just Donald Trump and his health secretary. James Linney blames the general environment of disinformation and distrust in science
item.dc:creator: James Linney

item.title: Just days to go!
item.description: Excerpt: Thanks to a few brilliant contributions, our fighting fund was boosted by an excellent £844 over the last week.
item.dc:creator: Robbie Rix

item.title: Letters
item.description: Trouble at t’SWP; Thatcher again; N20 fash bash; Blood booster
item.dc:creator: James Clifford
Ian Spencer
Tech Com

item.title: Online Communist Forum, Sunday November 29 5pm
item.description: Excerpt: One year after Liverpool: Your Party was always their party
item.dc:creator: Tina Becker

item.title: Time has run out
item.description: Antalya ended in complete failure. But the big victory scored by the oil producers and fossil fuel lobbyists underlines that the whole Cop merry-go-round has done nothing to halt the rise in global temperatures. Michael Roberts provides the damning facts and figures
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Two takes on a genocidal nightmare
item.description: Anne McShane reviews Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor (directors) NAZA. Daniele Rugo and Kyle Oakeson (directors) Life support. Both on general release
item.dc:creator: Anne McShane

item.title: USSR - A Marxist post-mortem: Internal contradictions
item.description: Excerpt: Jack Conrad uses the logic of Marxism to lay bare the Soviet Union’s inner laws Having done that, we begin to understand why the system showed such initial dynamism and yet inevitably tended towards stagnation and eventual collapse First of four books Paperback, pp679, £20 from:…
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: Wholly Jewish in implementation?
item.description: It is not western Jewry that is to blame for the ongoing genocide in Gaza. To say otherwise is to mistake the symptoms for the disease, says Tony Greenstein in his open letter to Susan Abulhawa
item.dc:creator: Tony Greenstein

item.title: If loving you is Huang …
item.description: The underlying dynamic, of dividing the world into great-power blocs pending great-power war, has been drastically reinforced by - of all things - the sexual exploits of a middle-aged, leather-jacketed nerd. Harley Filben looks at Nvidia and its strategic importance
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Letters
item.description: Friendly polemics?; Jobs for youth; Attack on youth; In the shredder; AXA targeted; Off UK soil!; Significant book
item.dc:creator: FRS

Action Network

item.title: Managing, not replacing capitalism
item.description: Price controls, buffer stocks and taxing the rich will not get beyond first base while finance, business and resources remain in private hands. Michael Roberts critiques ‘anti-fascist economics’
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Milburn’s recipe for social murder
item.description: Andy Burnham says no one need lose out when it comes to solving the ‘Neets crisis’. But the reality will be conscription into low-paid, dead-end jobs for the benefit of the least competitive sections of the capitalist class. Ian Spencer investigates
item.dc:creator: Ian Spencer

item.title: Online Communist Forum, Sunday November 22 5pm
item.description: Excerpt: After the Trump, Xi, Putin summit: political report from the CPGB’s Provisional Central Committee and discussion
item.dc:creator: Provisional Central Committee of the CPGB

item.title: Our vital work
item.description: Excerpt: Thanks once again to all those Weekly Worker supporters who continue to help finance the paper with their generous donations.
item.dc:creator: Robbie Rix

item.title: Question sacred ‘proof texts’
item.description: There are many who tail what they call the ‘movement’ in the name of some supposed ‘anti-sectarian’ orthodoxy. In reality this means refraining from harsh criticism and abiding by bureaucratic speech controls. Mike Macnair adds to last week’s reports of the Historical Materialism conference
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: Socialism, gentrification and abjection
item.description: Paul Demarty reviews Fredrik deBoer All in your head Simon & Schuster 2026, pp291, £20
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Thinking beyond the streets
item.description: Momentum is not being maintained and the left is often pointlessly divided. Yet, though the government is playing a waiting game, discontent has not dissipated. Jean Laurel calls for principled unity
item.dc:creator: Jean Laurel

item.title: Turn fear into active use
item.description: Calls for public ownership and democratic control are all well and good, but what about now? The left needs to embrace AI and employ it for our own purposes. As a first step, says Yassamine Mather, we need to know how the technology works. After that we can develop, master and apply
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Two corpses and a minghun wedding
item.description: No annual conference, no branches, no democracy. Now we are told Left Unity has affiliated. Carla Roberts reminds us that traditionally, in China, a ghost marriage sees reburial in a common grave
item.dc:creator: Carla Roberts

item.title: USSR - A Marxist post-mortem: Internal contradictions
item.description: Excerpt: Jack Conrad uses the logic of Marxism to lay bare the Soviet Union’s inner laws
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: Celebrity culture in the dock
item.description: With the conviction of Russell Brand on one count of rape and three of sexual assault, and now the David Walliams allegations, Paul Demarty calls for self-critical reflection on the left and a healthier, more egalitarian sexual culture
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Dancing the word
item.description: Jack Conrad reviews Chris Knight and Jerome Lewis The revolutionary origins of language New Haven CT 2026, pp384, hbk £25
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: Grappling with digital speed
item.description: Yassamine Mather dipped into the sessions on imperialism and Iran. The second session she attended was not only poorly presented, but the politics were awful. So, instead, she took to the ‘AI and capitalism’ stream. It proved much more interesting
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Letters
item.description: Yorp branch; Congress tactics; Priority reading; Former RCP; Scrap juries; French protests
item.dc:creator: Rafał B
Sam Moews
Frank Kavanagh
Lawrence Parker
Andrew Northall
Jim Moody

item.title: Low expectations
item.description: Reportedly, it was the economy that sank Trump and the Republicans in the midterms … that and the unpopular Iran war. Yet, even with a clear majority in both houses, the Democrats are not going to bring about major change. And then there is the AI bubble, says Michael Roberts
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Online Communist Forum, Sunday November 15 5pm
item.description: Excerpt: Cop31 - more fiddling while the planet burns: political report from the CPGB’s Provisional Central Committee and discussion
item.dc:creator: Provisional Central Committee of the CPGB

item.title: See us home
item.description: Excerpt: Once again, we’ve fallen well behind, when it comes to the Weekly Worker fighting fund. True, over the last week there were some very useful contributions, but overall, in the last seven days, a mere £234 has come into the kitty - less than a tenth of that £2,750 monthly target.
item.dc:creator: Robbie Rix

item.title: Setting terms in Congress
item.description: Democrats won more convincingly than expected in the midterms, and the DSA now has its eight-strong Bloc in Congress. There is also talk of a presidential run by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. How to navigate the coming challenges? DSA member Joseph Perez analyses the results and suggests ways forward
item.dc:creator: Joseph Perez

item.title: Slavery’s imperial apologists
item.description: Charles Windsor has not apologised for Britain’s role in Caribbean slavery. Nor has Andy Burnham. Mike Macnair says the official arguments against apologies and reparations are bogus. But to really right the wrongs of the past requires the overthrow of the world capitalist order
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: So much to choose from
item.description: Tam Dean Burn followed the ‘Culture’ stream. Walter Benjamin was very much mentioned. But what particularly struck him was the presentation given by Håkan Thörn and Carl Cassegård on postapocalyptic environmentalism
item.dc:creator: Tam Dean Burn

item.title: Strikes, streets and strategy
item.description: There have been massive protests of school and university students. November 5 took things to a higher level by mobilising the trade unions. What needs to happen next? Jean Laurel argues against the idea that rioting is positive, the way forward, something to celebrate
item.dc:creator: Jean Laurel

item.title: A hidden supreme leader
item.description: Irrationalist belief in divination, spirit contact, haloes and jinn armies grows above. Below, living standards are falling and protests are reviving. Yassamine Mather looks at the two worlds that make up the Islamic Republic
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: A long old road
item.description: Nigel with pet dog, Nigel posing as Kitchener, Nigel solving the pothole crisis. Edited by ex-leftist Mick Hume, Reform UK’s new paper has been launched. Paul Demarty reads it, so you don’t have to
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Bertolt Brecht and Holy Joy
item.description: Culture can bring together theatre, poetry, music, stand-up comedy, anthropology and communist politics. That, explains Tam Dean Burn, is the ambition of the Diderot Gesellschaft Movement
item.dc:creator: Tam Dean Burn

item.title: Help us get there
item.description: Excerpt: Before I report on the start of the November fighting fund, let’s just recap how we did in October. As I said last week, we had already exceeded the £2,750 monthly target, and the last couple of days saw another £58 come our way. Thanks to comrades BK (£25), JD and MD (£10 each)…
item.dc:creator: Robbie Rix

item.title: Letters

item.dc:creator: Provisional Central Committee of the CPGB

item.title: Revolutionary road to democracy
item.description: With the Democrats taking control of both houses of Congress and a much-expanded DSA contingent, it might appear that the US constitution has proven itself fit for socialist purposes. That is far from the case, argues Ian F. America needs a new, democratic, constitution
item.dc:creator: Ian F

item.title: Riot, loot and burn
item.description: France’s huge protest movement began with schoolers and now there is the November 5 general strike. Inevitably the disaffected, the backward, the plain criminal see an opportunity. However, says Jack Conrad, the task of Marxists is to raise consciousness, encourage organisation and inculcate discipline
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: The great AI swindle
item.description: Caught between faltering returns and lower-priced competition from China’s state-directed tech industry, the east Asian AI bubble is bursting. How will this affect the US? The big test will be the public launch of Anthropic, writes Michael Roberts
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Already £10 over
item.description: Excerpt: With still three days to go in October, I have some good news: the Weekly Worker has already reached our monthly £2,750 fighting fund target! Thanks to a very useful £582 that came our way over the last week, the running total currently stands at £2,760. Well done, everyone!
item.dc:creator: Robbie Rix

item.title: Letters
item.description: AI questions; Unfit SUTR; Cargo cult SWP; War fever; DSA tolerance; LFF, then CFF
item.dc:creator: Georg Tabor

item.title: Monumental crash beckons
item.description: Capitalist states face huge problems with high interest rates, low economic growth and ballooning government and corporate debt. Ted Reese says the system is in deep trouble and seems to be running out of options
item.dc:creator: Ted Reese

item.title: Nature cannot go ignored
item.description: There are still those on the left who say ‘labour creates all wealth’. Seemingly militant, seemingly pro-worker, seemingly anti-capitalist, but profoundly wrong, says Jack Conrad
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: New age of security chaos
item.description: PHP2Shell is the latest of many disastrous security vulnerabilities. Their discovery and exploitation are easier than ever in the age of AI. Buckle up, advises Paul Demarty
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: No clear outcome
item.description: There will be weeks of haggling, offers of bribes and ominous threats of all kinds. The Arab-majority parties might well be involved in this grubby business. But when it comes to the oppression of the Palestinians within and without Israel, no fundamental change should be expected, argues Yassamine Mather
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Online Communist Forum, Sunday November 1 5pm
item.description: Excerpt: Why we oppose rioting and looting: political report from the CPGB’s Provisional Central Committee and discussion
item.dc:creator: Provisional Central Committee of the CPGB

item.title: Pouvoir d’achat crisis
item.description: State education is in an advanced stage of decay. Over the last decade real spending per student has plummeted. Meanwhile the cost of living has soared, along with government borrowing costs. Michael Roberts investigates
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Readying for the next stage
item.description: November 5 sees the trade unions calling a general strike. It will be massive. Till then, argues Jean Laurel, the left needs to keep up the momentum of protests and demonstrations. The left also needs to promote the idea of the organised working class maintaining discipline and good order
item.dc:creator: Jean Laurel

item.title: Socialist Organiser to Resisting Socialism
item.description: From 1984 till his death, Alan Thornett was involved in almost every broad left front, coalition, alliance and party attempt. All quickly ended in failure, but lessons were never learnt. Mike Macnair concludes his two-part series
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: Banking on moonshots
item.description: Much to the alarm of the AI industry and interested governments, data centres face a growing tide of local opposition. Is this a reactionary attempt to roll back progress or a defensible popular revolt? Paul Demarty investigates
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: From militancy to the swamp
item.description: Alan Thornett, June 15 1937-October 9 2026, was one of those genuine rank-and-file leaders, a cadre steeled in the class struggles of Cowley car assembly plant. Having broken with the CPGB, he threw his lot in with Gerry Healy’s increasingly crazy outfit. After that, one failed merger followed another till he found the ‘lovely waters’ of Mandelism. Mike Macnair begins a two-part article
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: How to steal an election
item.description: Donald Trump’s Department of Homeland Security is conspiring to throw out millions of mail-in ballots under the guise of ‘election security’. Socialists must defend the right to vote, argues Nick D of the Marxist Unity Group. Socialists must also oppose the undemocratic system which enables the presidential dictatorship
item.dc:creator: Nick D

item.title: Letters
item.description: RSP censorsists; SNP rightists; Two-way Greens; DSA tankies
item.dc:creator: Jules Maximus
Tam Dean Burn
David Lindsay
Jon Hochschartner

item.title: Make up lost ground
item.description: Excerpt: What an excellent week for the Weekly Worker fighting fund. Incredibly, thanks to the support of our readers, we raised more in the last seven days than over the first two weeks!
item.dc:creator: Robbie Rix

item.title: Online Communist Forum, Sunday October 25 5pm
item.description: Excerpt: Chris Knight and Jerome Lewis introduce their groundbreaking book:
item.dc:creator: Chris Knight
Jerome Lewis

item.title: Programme for a kingdom
item.description: Among those expelled under the anti-communist proscribed list is Chris Williamson, the former Labour MP and former deputy leader of the Workers Party of Britain. Steve Freeman calls for his reinstatement and an urgent change of course
item.dc:creator: Steve Freeman

item.title: Rewarded for total failure
item.description: New Keynesian predictions about future economic activity have been way out of line. They have consistently got one thing wrong after another, says Michael Roberts. It is, therefore, fitting that Robert Hall and Michael Woodford have been handed this year’s Nobel prize in economics
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Seven you need to watch
item.description: Over 200 feature films and shorts were showcased over October 7-18 at the 70th annual London Film Festival. As with every year, there were some duds, a few shocks, but many treats. Jim Moody picks his particular highlights
item.dc:creator: Jim Moody

item.title: Who we support in Russia
item.description: While it is correct to oppose Nato’s proxy war in Ukraine, we cannot support Russia or ignore the reactionary nature of Putin’s dictatorial regime. Instead, argues Yassamine Mather, we should look to the anti-war left
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Achieving the good life
item.description: Did Keynes really have the solution to economic slumps, stagnation and mass unemployment? The majority of liberal left economists, trade union leaders and politicians think so. But, says Michael Roberts, it should not be back to Keynes, rather forward to Marx
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Do what you can
item.description: Excerpt: Last Saturday’s mass pro-Palestine demonstration in London was excellent in two senses: firstly, of course, for the huge numbers - including thousands of self-identifying Jews - expressing their opposition to the ongoing Israeli genocide; but also for the positive response from…
item.dc:creator: Robbie Rix

item.title: Modern wars, ancient myths
item.description: As the flame of war spreads across the region, Yassamine Mather looks at Saudi Arabia’s vulnerability, the misinformation surrounding the Houthis and Marco Rubio’s dangerous clash of civilisations nonsense
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Online Communist Forum, Sunday October 18 5pm
item.description: Excerpt: What is going on with Ukraine? Political report from the CPGB’s Provisional Central Committee
item.dc:creator: Provisional Central Committee of the CPGB

item.title: Postcard from the future
item.description: A Godzilla El Niño could persist until at least early next year, bringing record temperatures along with more flooding and drought. But there is also a possibility, paradoxically, that it could trigger a deep freeze in Europe, writes Eddie Ford
item.dc:creator: Eddie Ford

item.title: Prisoners in soft captivity
item.description: Does British promotion of European rearmament against Russia amount to a viable alternative to US domination? Mike Macnair does not think so. Europe is incapable of independent action
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: Soft left strengthens Vox
item.description: Housing, migration and the prospect of the hard right entering government for the first time since 1975 are the dominant issues, says Paul Davies. But what about the democratic republic, Nato and working class rule?
item.dc:creator: Paul Davies

item.title: The last man of ideas
item.description: Paul Demarty reviews Francis Fukuyama In the realm of the last man London 2026, pp304, £20
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Three years of genocide
item.description: Millions marched worldwide, in London over 200,000. No one is fooled by Ed Miliband’s weasel words, not least because of the continued arms trade with Israel and the ban on Palestine Action, says Ian Spencer
item.dc:creator: Ian Spencer

item.title: Why Israel is a racist state
item.description: We reprint this article by Moshé Machover in light of the media-amplified campaign against Green Party activists for daring to categorise Zionism as a form of racism. It most certainly is. As with any colonial-settler project, Zionism involves systemic discrimination against the indigenous population. First published in September 2018 by Labour Party Marxists
item.dc:creator: Moshe Machover

item.title: Youth take the lead
item.description: High schoolers have blockaded their schools and taken to the streets in unprecedented numbers. They have been joined by university students, teachers and parents. And on November 5 there is the call for a one-day general strike and mass demonstrations. Jean Laurel reports
item.dc:creator: Jean Laurel
